function.name: give_up
function.arguments: {"reason": "With one model call left the block is still on the table beside the bowl: the wrist view shows the bowl interior empty and the fixed views show the block still on the table. I spent the last calls on three close attempts (all latched fully closed, empty) and a levering sweep that pushed the block along the table but did not get it over the rim, so the pick-and-place cannot be completed within the remaining budget.", "hindsight": "Concrete facts about this rig: (1) move_to executes only 2-4 control steps (~1-2 cm of travel) per call no matter how large the requested delta is; distance to the target barely matters, so plan on ~1-2 cm of progress per model call. (2) Calls that include a gripper command run ~80 control steps and DO settle the full position target, so position goals should be bundled into the gripper open/close calls (e.g. open while sliding to the next x). (3) The block sits roughly 5 cm in +x from the start pose and the bowl ~5 cm further +x (bowl center near x=0.04, y~0.01); z of the end-effector must go to about 0.845 before closing, because at eef z>=0.86 the jaws close above the block top and latch fully shut on air. (4) The wrist camera stops showing the block when it is directly under the TCP (self-occlusion), so its absence there is not evidence of a miss; the front view keeps the block centered under the arm in x-image even when the jaws miss laterally, so y cannot be read reliably from the fixed views. (5) A closed-jaw sweep along +x pushes the block along the table toward the bowl but wedges it against the bowl outer wall instead of putting it in; a low push cannot climb the rim. (6) The gripper measurement ~0.016 normalized means the jaws met with nothing between them; a held block reads ~0.3-0.5."}
